description: Equipo de estudiantes de ingeniería pertenecientes al equipo de MotoStudent de la Universidad de Sevilla, eUSRACING. Apasionados por el espacio, el diseño y la propulsión.
summary:
FLAMA (Flame in Freefall) is a web dashboard that turns NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion data into fire-safety guidance for crewed spacecraft and habitats. It is built only on the 24 PSI combustion investigations: their official records, 21 experimental tables and the full PSI catalogue. Every figure and claim links back to the exact record or table it comes from.

It has five parts:

- Most Relevant Investigations: ranks the PSI investigations for a given scenario.
- Safety Mechanisms: scores the studies that most directly help prevent, detect or suppress a cabin fire.
- 3D cabin simulator: compares ISS, Gateway, lunar, Martian and EVA conditions.
- Theory Lab: finds patterns across the whole archive, keeping only hypotheses backed by at least ten investigations.
- Llama: a voice and text AI assistant that answers astronaut scenarios from the PSI tables and cites its sources.

Flammy, an on-screen advisor, turns each scenario into operational recommendations.

Fire is one of the most dangerous emergencies in spaceflight, and flames in microgravity or partial gravity do not behave as they do on Earth. As Artemis heads to the Moon with new oxygen and pressure settings, FLAMA makes decades of NASA combustion research searchable, explainable and traceable for mission planners, engineers and students.
details:
FLAMA is a web dashboard that turns NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion data into fire-safety guidance for crewed spacecraft and habitats. The data layer is the official PSI material, kept read-only:

- the records of the 24 combustion investigations;

- 21 experimental tables and the related test matrices;

- the full PSI catalogue of 133 investigations.

At startup the app indexes this data and builds a text library, so every record and table can be opened inside the app. Each number shown links back to the exact file it comes from.

The dashboard has five parts:

- Most Relevant Investigations: ranks the PSI investigations for the current scenario (gravity, oxygen, pressure, material).

- Safety Mechanisms: scores the studies that most directly help prevent, detect or suppress a cabin fire, using a transparent FLAMA Score.

- 3D cabin simulator: a spacecraft model where users compare ISS, Gateway, lunar, Martian, EVA and custom conditions. Smoke spread uses a simple advection–diffusion model, labelled as a conceptual visualization; every input value cites its PSI source.

- Theory Lab: an AI reads across the whole archive and proposes hypotheses. Each one is checked against verbatim quotes and kept only if at least ten investigations support it. It gets a probability from the evidence for and against, P = (S+1)/(S+C+2), plus a proposed microgravity experiment that could confirm it.

- Llama: a voice and text assistant. It queries the PSI tables and documents through tools, answers in the user’s language, draws charts, writes reports and cites the exact table or record behind each answer.

Flammy, an animated advisor, reacts to every action with operational recommendations backed by those sources.

Benefits and intended impact:

Fire is one of the most dangerous emergencies in spaceflight (Apollo 1, Mir), and flames in microgravity or partial gravity spread, extinguish and produce smoke differently from on Earth. The data needed to understand this exists, but it is spread across dozens of datasets that are hard to read. FLAMA makes it searchable, explainable and traceable in seconds. The intended users are:

- mission planners choosing cabin atmospheres for Artemis and lunar habitats;

- engineers screening materials and suppression strategies;

- students and the public learning how fire behaves in space.

Tools and technologies:

- Languages: Python, JavaScript, HTML and CSS.

- Web app: Streamlit, deployed on Streamlit Community Cloud with automatic redeploys from GitHub.

- Data: pandas and openpyxl to process the PSI data.

- 3D: Three.js, with a GLB spacecraft model.

- AI server: FastAPI with WebSockets, hosted on Render. It uses the Google Gemini Live API for real-time voice, and Gemini embeddings for retrieval over the PSI documents.

- Without an AI server: the chat falls back to a database-only mode that quotes the PSI files and computes figures from the tables, with speech recognition running in the browser (Web Speech API, or Whisper through transformers.js).

- Development: Git and GitHub, with AI-assisted development using Claude Code.

Creativity:

FLAMA combines a living character (Flammy), a 3D cabin, an AI that speaks and cites, and a theory engine that only accepts hypotheses backed by many independent experiments. Every element links back to the raw NASA data, so it is both engaging and verifiable.

Factors we considered:

- Scientific integrity: the PSI folder is read-only, nothing is invented, and anything not in the data is labelled “Conceptual”. The simulator never claims a fire probability.

- Traceability: every citation opens the exact source file.

- Cost and quotas: free tiers, rate limits on AI features, and a no-AI fallback.

- Security: API keys stay on the server.

- Licensing: Gemini terms of use for EU users, and the PSI’s CC0 data licence.

- Accessibility: mobile layout, reduced-motion support and voice input.

- Robustness: the app works offline from the data if the AI server is unavailable.
